PLAN 09 | SHOTS 22-23 | THE SHADOWS LOOSEN
Create a 15-second Seedance 2.5 cinematic sequence, horizontal 16:9. Exactly 2 shots with the local timing below. Preserve the assigned identities, masks, wardrobe, animal design and location geometry. Performance is expressed through posture, hands, breathing and weight. Render at natural speed with tactile analog texture.
CHARACTER REFERENCES
CHAR_SHAHRNAZ = {{CHAR_SHAHRNAZ}}
CHAR_ARNAVAZ = {{CHAR_ARNAVAZ}}
CHAR_ZAHHAK = {{CHAR_ZAHHAK}}
CHAR_GUARD_A = {{CHAR_GUARD_A}}
CHAR_GUARD_B = {{CHAR_GUARD_B}}
CHAR_GUARD_C = {{CHAR_GUARD_C}}
ANIMAL REFERENCES
ANIMAL_CAT = {{ANIMAL_CAT}}
LOCATION REFERENCES
LOC_ZAHHAK_HALL = {{LOC_ZAHHAK_HALL}}
PROP REFERENCES
PROP_STAFF = {{PROP_STAFF}}
PROP_BLADE = {{PROP_BLADE}}
START STATE AND BLOCKING
STATE_SHADOW_LOOSENING. The hall blocking matches block 08; guards remain half a pace behind and hands-off. Zahhak’s left palm stays open, right hand on staff. Both human shadows initially touch the sisters’ feet; the cat remains supported in Shahrnaz’s arms. Effect: flat darkness attached to the stone surface.

SHOT 22 | 00:00-00:08 | THE DELAY
40mm low oblique composition containing the sisters’ full bodies and their shadows toward Zahhak in the background. Camera creeps forward thirty centimeters. Arnavaz turns her head and shifts her shoulders; her floor silhouette responds half a beat late. Shahrnaz’s shadow begins to lengthen while her feet remain still. Ambient fill diminishes gradually.
SHOT 23 | 00:08-00:15 | FIRST SEPARATION
Cut to 50mm near floor level, keeping both pairs of feet and the direction toward Zahhak visible. A narrow gap opens between each human shadow and its feet. The two flat silhouettes slide a short distance along floor seams toward the staff. At the upper edge of frame Shahrnaz’s posture slackens; Arnavaz braces backward. Hold the cat securely against Shahrnaz’s torso.
LIGHT AND IMAGE
Over the first eight seconds gradually dim the existing practical fill while keeping the rear-left directional source fixed. Lock exposure so the dimming remains visible; floor seams remain readable beneath the darkening shadows.
SOUND
Breathing becomes prominent as room tone thins. Cloth tension at Arnavaz’s shoulders, one heel scraping stone, cat breath. The supernatural event is silent.
END STATE AND EDIT
Both human shadow silhouettes have separated slightly from the feet and stretch toward Zahhak. Shahrnaz’s shoulders slacken first; Arnavaz still leans backward. Bodies stay solid, grounded and on their marks. Light reaches a stable reduced level.
Keep all character designs and prop ownership consistent across cuts. Use the camera paths stated for each shot and retain readable spatial relationships. Primitive ritual fashion cinema, analog realism. NO MUSIC, NO DIALOGUE.

- PLAN 09 | SHOTS 22A–22C | THE INVASION OF PERSONAL SPACE

Create a 15-second cinematic sequence, horizontal 16:9.
Exactly three five-second shots.

CHARACTER REFERENCES:
Shahrnaz = {{CHAR_SHAHRNAZ}}
Arnavaz = {{CHAR_ARNAVAZ}}
Zahhak and his established shoulder serpents = {{CHAR_ZAHHAK}}

ANIMAL REFERENCE:
Cat = {{ANIMAL_CAT}}

LOCATION REFERENCE:
Zahhak’s chamber = {{LOC_ZAHHAK_HALL}}

PROP REFERENCE:
Zahhak’s staff = {{PROP_STAFF}}

Preserve every referenced mask, costume, body proportion and design.

FIXED SPATIAL MAP:

North and south describe the room, independently of the camera.

Zahhak begins north of the sisters, facing south toward them.
The sisters stand south of him, facing north.
Shahrnaz occupies the western mark.
Arnavaz occupies the eastern mark, seventy centimeters beside her.

Shahrnaz securely holds the cat against her chest.
Arnavaz’s left shoulder remains lowered; stone dust marks her left sleeve and lower garment.

Exactly three adults and one cat occupy the chamber. The guards have departed. The visible prop is Zahhak’s staff. The floor between the characters is open and continuous.

SHOT 22A | 00:00–00:05 | HE DETERMINES THE LIGHT

35mm handheld camera SOUTH of the sisters, looking NORTH.

Shahrnaz’s BACK occupies the left foreground.
Arnavaz’s BACK occupies the right foreground.
Zahhak faces the camera in the space between their shoulders, looking at the women rather than into the lens.

Zahhak takes one short staff-supported step toward them and stops.

The surrounding ambient light rapidly diminishes. After a brief pause, one hard overhead spotlight illuminates both sisters and a small area of floor around their feet.

Zahhak remains mostly outside this pool, his mask and staff catching narrow reflected highlights.

The camera edges forward between the sisters’ shoulder lines, maintaining their backs in the foreground.

SHOT 22B | 00:05–00:10 | TOO CLOSE

Cut to a 40mm camera NORTH of the sisters, just east of Zahhak, looking SOUTH.

The sisters’ masked FRONTS are visible:
Arnavaz appears on screen-left.
Shahrnaz appears on screen-right, holding the cat.

Zahhak’s BACK and right shoulder occupy the left foreground. His head turns toward Shahrnaz on screen-right.

He leans close to Shahrnaz’s mask without touching her. She draws her head backward, turns the cat slightly away from him and tightens her protective posture.

Arnavaz turns her masked face toward this intrusion.

The camera retreats a few centimeters with Shahrnaz’s recoil, using tense organic handheld movement. Preserve the eyeline connection between Zahhak and Shahrnaz.

SHOT 22C | 00:10–00:15 | BEHIND HER SHOULDER

Cut to a 35mm camera WEST of Shahrnaz, looking EAST across the sisters.

Shahrnaz is the near figure in profile, facing screen-left toward north.
Arnavaz stands deeper in the frame, beyond her.

Zahhak begins screen-left, in front of Shahrnaz. Show him physically passing around her western side, close to the lens, and arriving screen-right behind her shoulder.

His body briefly obscures the image during this passage. The camera makes a small lateral correction to recover Shahrnaz’s profile.

Zahhak lowers his mask close behind her head. Shahrnaz freezes and turns her head only slightly, afraid to complete the turn. Her breathing becomes rapid.

Arnavaz turns her head toward Zahhak’s new position while keeping her feet on her original mark.

End with Zahhak behind Shahrnaz, outside the strongest overhead light.

LIGHT AND PERFORMANCE:

One hard overhead spotlight contains the sisters within a shared pool. Peripheral architecture falls into near-black; retain narrow edge detail on Zahhak whenever he approaches them.

Zahhak moves slowly, with controlled shifts of his head and torso and the established slight limp. His physical route remains continuous.

The women’s fear appears through interrupted breathing, recoiling heads and protective hands. The cat remains supported and unsettled.

SOUND:
Staff contacting stone, short uneven breaths, restrained footsteps, cloth against fur and faint scale movement. The lighting change is silent.

NO MUSIC, NO DIALOGUE.
